description: Compute (a+b), (a−b), (a×b) and a^b modulo m, plus gcd(a,b) and the modular inverse — with the real number-theory algorithms underneath.

faqs.a: Modular arithmetic is arithmetic with a “wrap-around” modulus m: results are always reduced to the range 0…m−1, like hours on a 12-hour clock.

faqs.q: How is a^b mod m computed for large b?
faqs.a: With square-and-multiply (binary exponentiation), which needs only O(log b) multiplications instead of b multiplications, so even huge exponents finish instantly.

faqs.q: When does a modular inverse exist?
faqs.a: a⁻¹ mod m exists exactly when gcd(a, m) = 1, i.e. a and m are coprime. The tool uses the extended Euclidean algorithm and tells you when no inverse exists.

howto: Enter a, b and the modulus m (m must be positive for modular operations).
Choose the operation: add, subtract, multiply, power, gcd or modular inverse.
The result appears instantly, always in the range 0 to m−1 for modular operations.
Read the working note to see which algorithm was applied.
title: Modular Arithmetic Calculator
